title: Notification System
subtitle: A queue absorbs the load, and priority lanes stop a campaign from burying the one-time codes
motto: Deliver the important message first, and the rest when there is room
keyInsight: A queue only smooths spikes if the workers are sized for the peak, and even then one shared queue lets a 50-million-message campaign delay a login code by eight minutes until separate priority lanes reserve capacity for urgent traffic.

decisions.title: Start with workers sized for the average
decisions.description: The first frame sizes the fleet for the average rate to show a queue cannot hide a sustained peak: the backlog grows and one-time codes wait 24 minutes.
decisions.alternatives: Starting with the peak-sized fleet would make the queue look like the whole answer.

decisions.title: Fail on a campaign, not on a server
decisions.description: The failure frame is a marketing burst in a shared queue, because the damage is a broken latency promise for urgent messages and no server is down.
decisions.alternatives: A provider outage is the other failure; the vault handles it with retries, a dead letter queue and failover, so it is described and not simulated.

decisions.title: Reserve workers for high priority
decisions.description: The trade-off frame reports both the code delay that stays at about a second and the idle reserved capacity and slower campaign that pay for it.
decisions.alternatives: Reporting only the fast codes would make the reservation look free.
